title: SAHIWAL / BODY CONDITION SCORING
text:
SAHIWAL
Origin: Pakistan & India
Markings: Reddish brown to predominant red
Desirable Characteristics:
✓ Good maternal traits
✓ High resistance to parasites
✓ Well-developed udder
Performance:
✓ 425kg
✓ 4,000kg milk/year

BODY CONDITION SCORING

1 - Emaciated
The individual vertebrae of the spine are prominent. The short ribs are sharp to the touch and give a shelf-like appearance to the loin. The hook and pin bones of the pelvis are well defined. The anal area of the cow is receded displaying a prominent vulva. Considered unfit to travel.

2 - Thin
The short ribs can be felt but are less outstanding. The hook and pin bones are still well-defined, though the area around the anus is less sunken and the vulva is prominent.

3 - Average
The short ribs are palpable with slight pressure. There is no shelf-like appearance to this area. The spine and hook and pin bones are all rounded and smoothed over. The anal area is filled out, and there is no evidence of fat deposits.

4 - Heavy
The short ribs are rounded over with no evidence of a shelf-like appearance and may only be felt with firm palpation. The ridge of the backbone is flattened over the loin and rump areas. The hook bones are smoothed over and the area around the pin bones shows some fat deposits.

5 - Fat
The bone structures of the spine, hook and pin bones, and short ribs are not discernible. There are fat deposits around the tailhead and over ribs. The thighs curve out and the brisket and flanks appear to be very full and heavy.

facts: The Sahiwal breed originates from Pakistan & India.
The coat markings of the Sahiwal breed range from reddish brown to predominant red.
Desirable characteristics of Sahiwal include good maternal traits, high resistance to parasites, and a well-developed udder.
The typical weight performance of a Sahiwal cow is 425 kg.
The annual milk production performance of a Sahiwal cow is 4,000 kg milk/year.

In Body Condition Score (BCS) 1 (Emaciated), individual vertebrae of the spine are prominent, short ribs are sharp to the touch giving a shelf-like appearance to the loin, hook and pin bones are well defined, and the anal area is receded displaying a prominent vulva.
A cow with BCS 1 (Emaciated) is considered unfit to travel.
In BCS 2 (Thin), short ribs can be felt but are less outstanding, hook and pin bones are still well-defined, the area around the anus is less sunken, and the vulva is prominent.

In BCS 3 (Average), short ribs are palpable with slight pressure with no shelf-like appearance, spine and hook and pin bones are rounded and smoothed over, the anal area is filled out, and there is no evidence of fat deposits.

In BCS 4 (Heavy), short ribs are rounded over with no shelf-like appearance and felt only with firm palpation; the backbone ridge is flattened over loin and rump; hook bones are smoothed over and area around pin bones shows fat deposits.

In BCS 5 (Fat), bone structures of spine, hook and pin bones, and short ribs are not discernible; fat deposits exist around tailhead and over ribs; thighs curve out, and brisket and flanks appear very full and heavy.
